reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about segregation, melting-point depression, and the effect of pre-annealing in a five-component HEA nanoparticle system, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the segregation behavior or melting response of this specific complex alloy at the nanoscale.
premises: Copper segregates to the surface of Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles during high-temperature exposure
Surface copper enrichment locally depresses the melting point, initiating premelting
Pre-annealing homogenizes the elemental distribution and suppresses copper segregation
Homogenized nanoparticles exhibit a delayed, sharper melting transition akin to bulk behavior
Nanoscale phase-transition behavior in chemically complex nanoparticles is governed by surface segregation rather than other mechanisms
